title: Reg Marshall as booking agent: Los Angeles dates and the 5-4 Ballroom
summary: Reg Marshall got Fields into the Club Alabam after Kenton, the 5-4 Ballroom and Vancouver; Fields thought him honest because he wasn't big enough to cheat.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Marshal Royal, Reg Marshall booked you for a while; didn't he?

Oh, yes, Reg Marshall booked me quite a bit. I'm glad you thought of that, because I forgot about him. He got me some pretty nice spots, I mentioned I think, about Schoonover, that carried me west, but like sandlot and big league, Reg--
So Reg liked the sandlot to the big league?

I think Reg was responsible for me doing my first date in Los Angeles. I did the 5-4 Ballroom in Los Angeles-- no, it wasn't the first, I believe the first one was John Artis during the war, when I played at the Club Alabam, that was when Stan Kenton was just getting up. I think I followed Stan Kenton in the Club Alabam.
That was around about forty two or three or something like that because I remember the war was going on.
When Reg booked me, I didn't get back in there anymore until in the fifties, I played the 5-4 Ballroom. You remember that?
I played there the night they murdered Sullivan, Temptations. We got up to Monterey, California the next night and they killed him the next night in the 5-4 that night. That was in 1968, I guess.
Sullivan was older; what was Mr. Sullivan's first name?
Reg carried me on up to Seattle and then into Canada, did some dates for Reg in Vancouver.
How would you characterize Reg as a booking agent? As far as honesty and that type of thing.
Well, the way it was, to tell you the truth, I wasn't big enough--he didn't have a chance to cheat me. It was just in black and white what it was.
Yeah. There are a lot of ways that they have of doing it, drawing two contracts, but I doubt very seriously if he had one that was paying a little more than the one that I got.
You were quite big as the Basie and those others.
Yeah, that's when they could get to you, you know, when you get the percentage and this and that.
I'm not trying to imply that he was dishonest, Reg Marshall, but guys did have some things about him.
